alerts.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued November 25 at 11:54PM PST until November 27 at 10:00PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
alerts.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal
flooding with up to 2.5 feet of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways.
F For the Beach Hazards Statement, An increased risk for sneaker
waves and strong rip currents with breaking waves of 13 to 19 ft
expected.

* WHERE...Coastal North Bay Including Point Reyes National
Seashore, San Francisco Peninsula Coast, Northern Monterey Bay
and Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM PST
Thursday. For the Beach Hazards Statement, through Friday
evening.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning,
pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...These predictions are approaching the
highest tide ever recorded. At the San Francisco tidal gauge,
high tide is expected to be 2.2 ft above normal (8.0 ft MLLW) at
11:38 AM Thursday. These predictions include up to 1.5 ft of
surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding
threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along
the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay,
respectively.
alerts.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Stay off of jetties, piers, rocks, and other waterside
infrastructure. Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous surf
and NEVER turn your back on the ocean. Monitor local weather,
surf and tide forecasts at www.weather.gov/mtr.
